description:
This product is a professionally race-prepared track chain, optimised in-house by Velodrome.Shop for riders seeking ultra-low drivetrain friction, consistency under load, and maximum convenience.

You choose the chain. We apply the preparation.

What This Is

A brand-new, standard track chain selected from the product options in the menu above and professionally prepared after purchase using a controlled ultrasonic cleaning and wax-based race treatment process.

This is not a factory-modified chain and is not endorsed by the chain manufacturer. It is an optional race-preparation service for riders who choose a wax-based drivetrain setup.

Preparation Process

Each chain is prepared in-house using a repeatable, workshop-controlled process:

Multi-stage ultrasonic cleaning
to remove factory oils and contaminants

Hot-wax immersion
using CeramicSpeed UFO Speed Wax

Controlled cooling and manual articulation to ensure free movement of every link

Supplementary solid lubricant treatment
using ultrafine molybdenum and tungsten disulfide powders, commonly used in high-load mechanical systems to support boundary lubrication

The result is a clean, dry, low-friction chain optimised for indoor velodrome use and race-day performance.

Why Solid Lubricant Additives Are Used

Under extreme loads — such as standing starts, sprint accelerations, and sustained pursuit efforts — wax films can become very thin at the pin and roller interface.

Fine solid lubricants such as molybdenum and tungsten disulfide are widely used in high-load applications to help support boundary lubrication when lubricant films are momentarily displaced. In a waxed chain system, these additives act as a complementary layer within the wax matrix rather than a permanent coating.

This service is intended for race-day optimisation in clean, controlled environments, such as indoor velodromes, it is not recommended to use the chains supplied with this service on a fixed gear road bike setup.

Important Notes

Factory-applied lubrication has been removed and replaced with a wax-based system

Waxed chains should not be lubricated with oil-based products

A very short bedding-in ride is recommended before key events

This is a race-prep service, not general maintenance advice

This is a convenience-led, professional race-preparation service for riders who want the benefits of a waxed chain without the equipment, solvents, or trial-and-error of home preparation.

Prepared correctly. Supplied ready to race at the highest level.

INSTALLATION

Pre-waxed chains are installed just as you would a normal chain, check the product description on the product page for the chain you have selected for detailed installation advice.

When using a split link etc ensure that the pins are clear of wax once inserted through the chain.

MAINTENANCE

Wax-based chain systems deliver their lowest friction during a defined peak performance window rather than indefinitely. Under high-load track conditions, this window is typically in the region of 200–400 km, depending on rider power, event type, and maintenance.

Beyond this point, friction levels gradually increase as the wax film wears, eventually approaching that of a well-maintained liquid-lubricated chain. The chain itself is not worn out; only the lubrication system has passed its peak efficiency.

For elite-level track racing, we recommend allocating one pre-waxed chain per major target event (for example, a World Championships week) to ensure maximum consistency and minimum drivetrain losses when it matters most.

After the event, the same chain can be rotated into training or lower-priority competition use, and then re-waxed as required.

Re-waxing restores performance and does not reduce the structural life of the chain when carried out correctly

Pre-Waxed Race-Prepared Track Chain – FAQs

What exactly am I buying?

You are buying a brand-new standard track chain (selected from the product options) that has been professionally race-prepared in-house by Velodrome.Shop using ultrasonic cleaning, hot wax, and solid lubricant additives. This is a preparation service applied after purchase, not a factory-modified chain.

Is this an Izumi / DID / CeramicSpeed etc product?

No. The chain itself is a genuine manufacturer product, but the waxing and preparation process is carried out by Velodrome.Shop following the specific guidance and training by CeramicSpeed.

Does this affect the manufacturer warranty?

No Velodrome.Shop will honour the original product warranty for a chain that we have waxed

Is this suitable for sprint events?

Yes, provided the chain is correctly prepared and bedded in. Many sprint programmes use waxed chains, but some riders prefer alternative lubrication methods for feel consistency. Lubricant choice is secondary to correct chain length, chainline, and tension.

Is this better for pursuit and bunch racing?

Waxed chains are particularly well suited to:

Individual Pursuit

Team Pursuit

Omnium and bunch race events

These disciplines benefit from consistent torque delivery, minimal contamination, and very low friction over sustained efforts.

How long does a pre-waxed chain last?

Wax-based systems have a peak performance window, typically around 200–400 km under high-load track conditions.After this, friction gradually increases towards that of a well-maintained liquid-lubricated chain. The chain itself is not worn out.

Do I need a new pre-waxed chain for every event?

For elite-level racing, many riders allocate one pre-waxed chain per major target event (for example, a World Championships week) to ensure maximum consistency. Afterwards, the chain can be rotated into training or lower-priority competition use and re-waxed as required.

How do I maintain the chain after purchase?

For ongoing maintenance and top-ups, use a wax-based drip treatment such as
CeramicSpeed UFO Drip Track Chain Treatment
. Do not apply oil-based lubricants to a waxed chain.

Should I bed the chain in before racing?

Yes. A short bedding-in period is recommended before key races, especially for sprint events, to allow the wax system to stabilise.

Can I use this chain outdoors?

This service is intended for indoor velodrome use.

Can the chain be re-waxed later?

Yes. Re-waxing restores performance and does not reduce the structural life of the chain when carried out correctly.

Why Chains Matter in Track Cycling

Chains are often the largest contributor to drivetrain friction in track cycling. A poorly optimised chain can waste 10–20W — enough to decide an Olympic medal. The Renold Track Chain was developed specifically to address these challenges, focusing on:

Maximum tensile stiffness – essential for 2000W+ sprint torque

Low-friction bearing surfaces – reducing power loss at high speed

Durability and reliability – engineered for multiple rounds at World Championships and Olympic Games

The Renold Velo wear gauge has been specifically designed to accurately measure chain elongation without the need to remove it. To avoid problems with running, the chain should be replaced before elongation reaches 1%.
This assessment of chain elongation has now been made quick and easy with the Renold Velo wear gauge and this simple maintenance step can improve efficiency and performance by replacing your chain when it is required!

The Renold wear gauge can be read as follows. The numbers at the gauge show the chain elongation in percent. If the gradation with a number on it fits between two rollers, the chain elongation has reached this value in percent. The first gradation means 0.5% chain elongation.

At 0.7% wear, replacement of the chain should be considered in order to maintain optimum performance

At 1.5% wear, immediate replacement of the chain is indicated in order to prevent the risk of damage to machinery or potential injury
